clue.text: Relative gloomy about the form in which the title appears

definitions.text: form in which the title appears

parts.note: MA, mother, is a close relative

indicators.note: about means the word for gloomy wraps around the next piece

explanation.surface: Some sour relative broods over the format in which a book's title is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's masthead is the block at the top of the front page carrying its name.

clue.text: City men make reliable bets after March 10 reform

indicators.note: after places the betting piece behind the rearranged month and number
reform tells us to rebuild the letters of March and ten into a new shape

parts.note: bankers are near-certain bets, as on a football pools coupon

explanation.surface: Some City financiers are told to place safe wagers once a March overhaul is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges MARCH and TEN into MERCHANT. 'The City' is London's financial district, so City men are financiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant bankers work in the City of London, the capital's financial district, so they are archetypal City men.

clue.text: It is sweet to tease us in return

indicators.note: in return means the whole run of letters from tease and us is read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone protests that teasing us back is a kindly gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns RAGUS around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is the sweetener in tea and cakes, the very thing that tastes sweet.

clue.text: Teacher put over classes for listeners.

indicators.note: put over places the teacher above the classes in this down answer

parts.note: the head is the senior teacher of a school
sets are classes grouped by ability

explanation.surface: A head teacher takes charge of the school's sets for its pupils who listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Headsets are earphones worn by people listening to radio or recordings.

clue.text: Surrounded by and included in the team on good form

annotationWithheld.why: Surrounded by and included in the team on good form (5): no parse of 'the team on good form' gives AMONG; the clue seems garbled in the OCR text
annotationWithheld.clue: Surrounded by and included in the team on good form

clue.text: Merits being broadcast because he is a hitter

indicators.note: being broadcast suggests the letters of merits are scattered and reset

explanation.surface: A boxer's virtues are spread about by the press because he punches hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiter is one who strikes, so a hitter; the old verb smite means to hit hard.

clue.text: Crazy about a girl so flirted

indicators.note: about tells us the word for crazy encloses the girl

parts.note: she stands for any girl or woman

explanation.surface: A lovesick admirer, wild about a girl, made eyes at her.
explanation.definitionFit: To mash was old slang for to flirt or make amorous advances; a masher was a ladies' man.

clue.text: The man of ideas is the one who makes a revolt about nothing

indicators.note: about means the rebel phrase goes around the zero

parts.words: the one who makes a revolt
parts.note: a riser is someone who rises up in revolt; with the it gives the riser
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A thinker is cast as a rabble-rouser stirring up trouble over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A riser is one who rises in revolt, so 'the one who makes a revolt' is read as a whole phrase, article included.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser forms theories, so is a thinker, a person of ideas.

clue.text: A feeble cry to arts might come from one of these boards

indicators.note: might come from suggests the letters of the feeble cry are reworked into the answer

explanation.surface: A weak plea for culture is heard from one of the long tables at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'one of' only join; the fodder is FEEBLE CRY TO ARTS, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board; refectory tables are the long ones in a monastery or college dining hall.

clue.text: Obliged to live with a bird but interrupted by the senile

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: interrupted by means the bird is broken open and the old age word is put inside

explanation.surface: Someone feels bound to keep a hen even though doddery old folk keep butting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholden means indebted, under an obligation to someone.

clue.text: Fix up graduate with part in rambling discourse

parts.note: to rig is to fix up or set up
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A drama graduate is cast in a long-winded speaking part.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, rambling or confused story or procedure.

clue.text: Spinsterhood for woman cut short by, fairy

indicators.note: cut short means the woman word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman is told her single life is curtailed by a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'by' is an OCR stray.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman left on the shelf is one thought past marrying, so the shelf stands for spinsterhood.

clue.text: A hothead, given weapons, does damage

parts.note: the head of hot is its first letter, H

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered man who is handed guns will hurt people.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm is to hurt or injure, so harms means does damage.

clue.text: Eric got me involved in using simple figures

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of Eric got me are tangled up

explanation.surface: Eric got me caught up in something using basic shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric patterns are built from simple shapes such as lines, circles and triangles.

clue.text: The flower comes near with a note about a fish

indicators.note: about means the musical note goes around the fish

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the shad is a fish of the herring family

explanation.surface: A flower is brought close, with a musical note written about a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes' is only a link; 'near' is the first piece, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightshade is a flowering plant, the deadly kind being belladonna.

clue.text: A great dud reformed and passed an exam

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of a great dud are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A hopeless student mended their ways and got through the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate is to finish a course of study and gain a degree after passing the final exams.

clue.text: Man, it's a dicey business making the airport!

parts.note: a throw of the dice is a dicey business

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that getting to the airport is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicey' is meant literally here: a throw of the dice. HEATHROW is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's busiest airport, the airport for most British travellers.

clue.text: Capital made from two slot machines

indicators.note: made from tells us the answer is formed from a run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A city's wealth is earned from a pair of one-armed bandits.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: The man to score freely when out in the open

indicators.note: freely means the letters of score are let loose in a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer scores at will when playing outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is Italian borrowed into English for in the fresh air, outdoors.

clue.text: Light piece of wood

definitions.meaning: a ray or shaft of light
a long thick timber in a building's frame

explanation.definitionFit: A beam is both a shaft of light and a heavy timber joist.

clue.text: A lord but for him fortune lay in obscurity

indicators.note: in obscurity hints that the letters of fortune lay are jumbled and hidden in a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman whose riches were once unknown to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the story: Little Lord Fauntleroy is a poor American boy who learns he is heir to an English earldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Lord Fauntleroy is the boy lord of Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel.

clue.text: Fruit which is almost enough for beating

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: pipping is beating someone by the narrowest margin, just enough to win

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is nearly enough to whip someone with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final G of PIPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A pippin is a variety of eating apple, such as Cox's Orange Pippin.

clue.text: Feeds the girls after I hurry back carrying a duck

indicators.note: after places the girls behind the I
carrying means the reversed hurry word holds the duck inside it
back means the word for hurry is read backwards

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O
shes is a jokey plural of she, so the girls

explanation.surface: Someone serves the girls their meal once they hurry back home with a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUN into NUR, and 'carrying' puts O inside to give NOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed and sustain.

clue.text: Queen's place for woman with a degree

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A woman with a degree is given a royal post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba ruled the biblical land of that name, so it is her kingdom.

clue.text: Unusual degree — is given for dancing

definitions.note: a gerund standing for a style of dance

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A strange qualification is handed out for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, one form of dancing.

clue.text: Damp as Nigella?

parts.note: Nigella is the garden flower love-in-a-mist; read as letters, love (zero, the letter O) sits inside a word for fine drizzle, giving a word for damp

explanation.surface: A question about whether a celebrity cook is looking a little sweaty.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella is not the cook but the plant whose common name is love-in-a-mist; in crosswords love is O, a zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, the same as damp.

clue.text: Prevent vessels returning to the east

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

indicators.note: returning means the word for vessels is read backwards

explanation.surface: Ships are kept from sailing back to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to bar or prevent someone from doing something.

clue.text: Excess population so some play with a means of reducing it

parts.note: overs are spells of play in cricket, six balls each
the contraceptive pill is a way to cut the population, the it of the clue

explanation.surface: Overcrowding is so bad that a little family planning is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some play' points to OVERS, units of a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is surplus population moved out of a crowded city into new towns.

clue.text: Track partisanship?

definitions.meaning: a short railway line beside the main one
taking one party's part in a dispute

explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a railway branch, and siding with someone is taking their part.

clue.text: Means of securing man's exit when the entrances are full of rubbish

indicators.note: full of means the entrances enclose the rubbish word

explanation.surface: A way out is secured when the doorways are choked with junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A garotte is a cord or wire for strangling, a grim means of ending someone's life.
